submit_request.description: One ordinary producer Event with the approval signatures its two approval layers require for the Event action or for this registered submit operation, or one atomic MLS Commit plus all recipient Welcome deliveries required by that Commit. The ordinary branch is EventAdmissionSubmission itself, not a second declaration of it: the approval evidence a constraint demands has to be carriable on the primary ingress, otherwise no execution could ever satisfy the constraint (zh/authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.2.5).

self_submit_request.description: Closed self Event-submit union. Ordinary Event and MLS Commit requests retain their current canonical shapes. Ordinary Realm bootstrap, Direct Conversation founding and membership compensation are the only aggregate branches; all are closed and are rejected on every other Event-submit endpoint.

self_submit_outcome.description: Closed self Event-submit outcome union. Aggregate outcomes cannot be parsed as an ordinary single-Event outcome.

peer_submit_request.description: The only peer Event ingress. branch is a semantic discriminator, not a routing hint: authority_forward performs first admission at the current governance Station; committed_replication stores source-committed replicas; registered_atomic_unit performs one registered all-or-nothing materialization. Bodies cannot be reinterpreted across branches. producer_device_evidence is allowed only on authority_forward and its presence is decided by the Event, not by the forwarder: it MUST be present when the actual signer (executed_by when present, otherwise actor_id; the Commit Event for mls_submission) is an Account whose proof verification_method fragment is an ak:device: id, and MUST be absent otherwise. The schema cannot express that Event-dependent rule, so the governance Station enforces it after producer resolution and rejects a missing or surplus member with schema_violation and zero writes (zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 8.2.2). mls_genesis_material is likewise allowed only on the authority_forward event branch, and there the Event kind alone decides it: required for ak.mls.genesis, forbidden otherwise. producer_agent_evidence is required exactly when the actual producer is an Agent runtime key; it is forbidden for human-device and service producers and on committed_replication/registered_atomic_unit. Missing, surplus or simultaneous device/Agent evidence is schema_violation with zero writes. Complete AccountId, runtime method/key, ASRE content ref, state and independent controller gate must all match. Missing compact cache is dependency_missing; no extra fetch endpoint. producer_agent_evidence is required exactly when the actual producer is an Agent runtime key; it is forbidden for human-device and service producers and on committed_replication/registered_atomic_unit. Missing, surplus or simultaneous device/Agent evidence is schema_violation with zero writes. Complete AccountId, runtime method/key, ASRE content ref, state and independent controller gate must all match. Missing compact cache is dependency_missing; no extra fetch endpoint.

mls_genesis_material.description: authority_forward event branch only. Required when event_submission.event.kind is ak.mls.genesis and forbidden for every other kind: the raw GroupInfo and ratchet_tree bytes of the two content-addressed Blobs the Genesis references, read by the forwarding Station (the creator's Account Station) from its own Blob store. The governance Station hashes each under its ref's embedded suite, compares with the Genesis payload refs, rejects a mismatch with digest_mismatch and zero writes, and stores both as public Blobs inside the acceptance transaction (zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md section 5.1.2).

producer_device_evidence.description: authority_forward only. Complete account_device evidence for a cross-Station human device producer, freshly signed by the forwarding Station (the producer's account Station) from the same durable cut as its live gate before every forwarding attempt and persisted with its ref before sending; never a cached or keys/query-returned object. The governance Station verifies Source-Service-ID equals attestation.account_id.station_id, the attestation signature under the carried Service history at attested_at, now earlier than attestation expires_at, the original authorization_window covering both Event created_at and now, device_status active, and exact producer AccountId/device fragment/key binding, and persists the complete object and ref inside the acceptance transaction for audit only. An exact duplicate Event returns its original outcome before evidence freshness is checked. event_authorization is required, covers the exact original Event and destination/canonical body, and freezes independent original authorization coordinates, revision, PCR tenure and source accepted_at. The complete evidence remains private audit; only the separately committed minimal fact is replicated.

peer_submit_outcome.description: Closed peer Event-submit outcome union. Replication reports one same-order item result for every input; registered units report exactly one indivisible outcome.

committed_event_submission.description: One exact source canonical Event inside an EventAdmissionSubmission containing only event, paired with the source-signed RealmCommit that accepted it. Private approval_signatures are forbidden on committed replication and stay in the governance Station's accepted-at audit. event_submission.event.event_id MUST equal source_commit.event_ref; realm and stream coordinates, governance generation, current source authority signature and previous_commit_ref continuity MUST verify exactly. The receiver does not redo the source admission approval. This shape accepts only the full producer Event, never a withheld or projection-only read view. For every ak.mls.commit, genesis_event_ref is required, frozen from the exact accepted group Genesis in the governance acceptance transaction, and covered by the authenticated canonical peer request; it is forbidden for other kinds. The receiver binds it to the exact Commit and immutable group provenance in the same replica transaction and never infers it from base_group_state_ref. welcomes is allowed only when the source Event is ak.mls.commit and carries exactly the MlsWelcomeDelivery objects of that Commit whose recipients the destination Station hosts, in submission order; the destination re-verifies each claim against its own claim ledger and queues the passing Welcomes in the same replica transaction as the Commit (zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md section 2.2). Every source Commit carrying producer_signer_fact_digest requires exactly this immutable Human fact; a fact without the digest is forbidden. Receiver checks exact Event/actual producer/device/method, original Commit digest and true Event Ed proof, retaining fact with canonical Event/Commit atomically. The fact does not replace admission/current membership or approval evidence.

event_submission.description: Only the exact source Event; approval_signatures is forbidden in committed replication and remains in the governance Station's private accepted-at audit.

genesis_event_ref.description: Immutable exact accepted Genesis EventId for the effective scope and MLS group of an ak.mls.commit. Required for every replicated MLS Commit, forbidden otherwise; signed peer-body metadata, not a recipient guess or a replacement for governance-side provenance verification.

welcomes.description: Exact producer-signed Welcome deliveries of this ak.mls.commit for recipients hosted by the destination Station, written into this outbox intent by the governance Station inside the Commit acceptance transaction. Absent for every other Event kind and when the destination hosts no recipient of the Commit.

mls_genesis_material.description: Raw epoch-0 public material of one forwarded ak.mls.genesis: the exact bytes of the GroupInfo and ratchet_tree Blobs named by the Genesis payload group_info_ref and ratchet_tree_ref, as unpadded base64url. It carries no ref or digest echo; the refs in the signed Genesis are the only digest carrier. Each member is at most 5592406 characters, so each decodes to at most 4194304 bytes and the two together never exceed 8388608 bytes, the ak.peer.mls.read.group_state_material.v1 response bound; a longer member is schema_violation and there is no separate aggregate bound.

peer_committed_replication_outcome.description: Per-item replication outcome. replication_outcomes has exactly the same length and order as request.replications. Input order identifies each row, so an outcome does not repeat an index or source coordinates. rejected means that item was not stored. Transport retry replays the complete request body and returns the same outcomes. This branch has no accepted finality vocabulary.

ordinary_realm_bootstrap_unit_submission.description: Self-only ordinary Collaboration Realm bootstrap. The caller submits the complete registered ordered unit to one current governance Station. Slot 0 derives the Realm ID; all following Events use that Realm and the same actor authority. The optional alias and conditional plaintext-visible-services slots retain registry order. The Station validates all slots against staged state, then atomically stores one consecutive RealmCommit per Event, every registered typed result, idempotency outcome and outbox or stores none. No batch-level authority artifact or receipt exists.

idempotency_key.description: UUIDv7 whole-unit replay fence. Same key and identical canonical request return the original ordered RealmCommits; same key with different request bytes is duplicate_conflict.

events.description: Exactly the ordinary_collaboration ordered slots in contract-registry.json.realm_bootstrap_registry. Runtime validation also checks the conditional visibility slot, all producer/approval proofs, staged authority-root evidence, exact Realm and actor bindings, and the final creator join.

ordinary_realm_bootstrap_creator_join_su.description: The final slot is the genesis actor's explicit member.state join with expected_revision null; the Station verifies payload and actor bindings against slot 0.

ordinary_realm_bootstrap_acceptance_outc.description: One indivisible ordinary Realm bootstrap outcome. The ordered commits match the submitted Events and form one consecutive source Realm stream chain. Exact whole-unit replay returns the same commits. No per-item partial success or batch-level receipt exists.

direct_conversation_founding_unit_submis.description: Self-only caller-authored Direct Conversation founding unit. The current Station recomputes authority from current evidence and therefore rejects a founding_authority_evidence echo. The four Events are accepted atomically in this exact order with consecutive RealmCommits: realm create, founder join, peer join, strand create. realm_id is retyped from events[0].event.event_id and main_strand_id from events[3].event.event_id.

idempotency_key.description: UUIDv7 founding-slot fence. Byte-identical replay returns the same four byte-identical source RealmCommits without changing the fourth committed_at; the same key with different canonical unit bytes is duplicate_conflict.

allOf.description: payload action MUST be join. The first occurrence is the founder and the second is the peer; the pair and Realm bindings must match the realm-create Event.

direct_conversation_founding_federation_.description: Peer-only source-committed Direct Conversation founding unit. The four committed rows have the same Event order as the self unit; their source commits have one Realm/generation/stream, consecutive positions and exact previous_commit_ref linkage. The receiver derives every coordinate from the four Events, verifies the source commits and bounded authority evidence, then materializes all four rows or none without re-signing commits or creating fanout. No second acceptance receipt or finality object exists.

direct_conversation_founding_acceptance_.description: One indivisible Direct Conversation founding outcome. Self first success, peer success and exact replay return the same four verified source commits. The commits are ordered like the unit and form one consecutive source chain; the fourth committed_at is the founding acceptance time. No receipt or per-item partial result exists.

peer_registered_atomic_unit.description: Closed registry of peer source-committed atomic units. Every listed unit is persisted and materialized all-or-nothing and produces no new Arkret Event finality.

membership_compensation_unit_submission.description: Self-only membership compensation aggregate. The enclosed Event is an ak.member.state leave/remove whose authorization_ref equals evidence.delegation.delegation_id. Evidence is transport-only and excluded from Event canonical bytes. The destination authority claims (admission_id, delegation_id) once in the same transaction as Event acceptance; mismatch, already absent, prior use or a superseding J2/new join is membership_compensation_conflict with zero writes.

membership_compensation_federation_submi.description: Peer-only source-committed membership compensation unit. The receiver verifies the full source Event/Commit pair and the unchanged compensation evidence, then atomically claims the same single-use binding and stores the source fact without re-signing a commit or fanout.

membership_compensation_evidence.description: Closed transport-only compensation evidence. The verifier recomputes delegation_id as ak:membership_compensation_delegation:sha256:<lowercase_hex SHA-256(JCS(core))>, verifies both signatures and exact join/admission/commit/executor bindings, and compares single_use_binding byte-for-byte. It is never inserted into Event canonical bytes.

membership_compensation_acceptance_outco.description: Atomic compensation outcome. committed and duplicate both carry the one authority-signed source commit. Exact full-body replay returns the same outcome; no per-item partial exists.

direct_conversation_founding_dependency_.description: Closed HTTP 409 application/problem+json response for a registered Direct Conversation founding unit whose bounded exact dependencies are not locally available. It is retryable only after canonical backfill/resolve and a new full-body request evaluation; no partial unit write occurred.

x-arkret-external-literal-object.specification: RFC 9457 Problem Details for HTTP APIs
x-arkret-external-literal-object.reason: The closed endpoint problem retains the RFC literal type/title/status/detail/instance member vocabulary and adds one registered details member.

stream_scan_request.description: Positional single-stream scan request. Pagination is by stream_position, not by an opaque cursor: within one stream the governance Station's stream_position is a strict +1 total order, so the position IS the continuation token. Exactly one of after_position / before_position MUST be present; the exclusivity is structural (the oneOf below), so a request carrying both or neither is a schema violation and MUST NOT be repaired by picking a default direction. Both bounds are read inside the range this caller is permitted to read, never over the physical stream: null means 'from the oldest position this caller may read' (after_position) or 'from the newest position this caller may read' (before_position). Continuation is the caller's job: take the largest stream_position of this batch for after_position, the smallest for before_position.

after_position.description: Scan toward newer commits: return commits whose stream_position is strictly greater than this value, ascending. null starts at the oldest position this caller may read, which is position 0 only when that floor is the physical stream start; see stream_scan_outcome.readable_floor.

before_position.description: Scan toward older commits (history backfill): return commits whose stream_position is strictly smaller than this value, descending. null starts at the newest position this caller may read, which is not necessarily the physical stream head. The scan stops at the caller's readable floor; positions below that floor are unreadable rather than missing and are not a gap (zh/sync/client-sync.md section 12.3.3).

readable_floor.description: Verifiable bottom of one caller's readable range on one stream. The anchor lets a member whose history is trimmed verify that its permitted prefix is complete without ever holding position 0: it proves where the accepted chain that caller may read begins, and it proves nothing about whether the Station holds further history below it or further updates above it.

oldest_position.description: Smallest stream_position this caller is permitted to read. Positions below it are unreadable, not missing: their absence MUST NOT be treated as a gap and MUST NOT be used to infer activity, membership or existence below the floor.

floor_commit_id.description: commit_id of the RealmCommit at oldest_position, so the boundary binds to the chain the caller has already accepted. The commit at the floor is the only readable commit allowed to carry a previous_commit_ref the caller cannot resolve, because its predecessor is outside that caller's range.

floor_reason.description: Why the range starts here. stream_start means the floor is the physical start of the stream and oldest_position is 0; the other two are trimmed ranges and MUST NOT be reported as stream_start. Retention never moves a floor: v1 never deletes an accepted RealmCommit and expired Events are returned through the withheld CommittedEventView branch.

stream_scan_outcome.description: Positional scan result over caller-visible committed Event views. There is no cursor or cross-stream order; continuation uses stream_position from committed_events[].

committed_events.description: Contiguous caller-visible committed Event views for the requested stream, ordered by RealmCommit stream_position. Full and withheld rows preserve the same verifiable Commit chain.

readable_floor.description: Verifiable bottom of this caller's readable range on the requested stream. It MUST be present on every page whose scan reached that bottom (a before_position page with truncated false, and an after_position page whose first row is at it), MAY be present on any other page of the same stream, and MUST be omitted only when the caller may read no commit of this stream at all, which is also the only case in which an empty committed_events[] with truncated false is legal.

truncated.description: True when at least one further commit that this caller is permitted to read exists beyond this page in the requested direction, i.e. the scan stopped on limit. It is a statement about the caller's permitted range, never about the physical stream: a scan that stopped on the newest readable position (after_position) or on readable_floor.oldest_position (before_position) MUST set it false even when the Station holds further commits this caller may not read. History outside the caller's range MUST NOT set it, a page that stopped on the floor MUST NOT be presented as truncation, and truncated MUST NOT be used to conceal a floor. An empty committed_events[] with truncated false means the caller's permitted range is exhausted in that direction, never that the physical stream is empty or absent.

committed_event_ref.description: Closed exact reference to one authority-committed Event. All four coordinates are verified against the returned RealmCommit; none is a hint.

final_stream_heads.description: Private state-transfer manifest whose canonical digest equals handoff.final_stream_heads_digest. It is not included in the public authority bundle.

historical_signer_facts.description: Private complete canonical inventory at the frozen authority handoff cut: exact target set equals all imported digest-bearing Full Commit originals, without duplicates, missing or extra entries. Canonical order: JCS UTF-8 stream_ref, numeric stream_position, UTF-8 event_id, UTF-8 commit_id. Authority handoff covers all authorized streams; ordinary peer member floors remain separate. Existing request budget applies: limit_exceeded rejects without partial authority startup. No private PCR bodies. New handoffs require the inventory, including empty array.

human_historical_signer_fact.description: Minimal immutable original Human device signer source frozen in governance acceptance. Actual signing Account, independent authorization coordinates/revision/PCR tenure and source accepted time. No target CommitId/position, current permission, verified flag or private PCR bytes.

human_historical_signer_fact_entry.description: Complete target association derived only after the original governance Commit exists. Fact digest excludes this outer target.

peer_stream_scan_outcome.description: Peer-only authorized original rows plus original governance-Commit-bound Human signer facts. Includes bootstrap tail/cold scan/backfill. Full digest-bearing Human rows require exactly one ordered entry. Hidden/withheld/redacted/existing_original-without-digest/Agent/Service rows have no entry; association and complete source verification are runtime obligations.

committed_events.description: Contiguous caller-visible committed Event views for the requested stream, ordered by RealmCommit stream_position. Full and withheld rows preserve the same verifiable Commit chain.

readable_floor.description: Verifiable bottom of this caller's readable range on the requested stream. It MUST be present on every page whose scan reached that bottom (a before_position page with truncated false, and an after_position page whose first row is at it), MAY be present on any other page of the same stream, and MUST be omitted only when the caller may read no commit of this stream at all, which is also the only case in which an empty committed_events[] with truncated false is legal.

truncated.description: True when at least one further commit that this caller is permitted to read exists beyond this page in the requested direction, i.e. the scan stopped on limit. It is a statement about the caller's permitted range, never about the physical stream: a scan that stopped on the newest readable position (after_position) or on readable_floor.oldest_position (before_position) MUST set it false even when the Station holds further commits this caller may not read. History outside the caller's range MUST NOT set it, a page that stopped on the floor MUST NOT be presented as truncation, and truncated MUST NOT be used to conceal a floor. An empty committed_events[] with truncated false means the caller's permitted range is exhausted in that direction, never that the physical stream is empty or absent.
